The document below is the pipeline run end to end. It is a single reproducible
R Markdown file: one configuration block at the top switches it between a binary
and a continuous outcome, and expensive steps are cached so that re-running after
an edit takes seconds rather than hours.

:::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
It is a large document with its own table of contents. Open it in a new tab and
use the sidebar to move between parts.
::::

[Open the full analysis →](output/full-analysis.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

## What is in it

| Part | Contents |
|---|---|
| **Setup and Configuration** | Package installation, source files, the caching helper, and the single global configuration block |
| **Part I. A "fit-the-fit" approach** | **1.1** BART estimation of conditional average treatment effects, with the per-patient CATE plot and MCMC diagnostics · **1.2** Subgroup discovery via classification and regression trees (CART) · **1.3** Variable importance and interaction (VIVI) heatmaps |
| **Part II. Sensitivity analyses and cross-method comparison** | **2.1** Sensitivity of the CATE estimates to the BART prior specification · **2.2** Cross-method comparison against Bayesian Causal Forest, XGBoost T- and S-learners, and causal forest |
| **Part III. Treatment effect heterogeneity by prognostic score** | **3.1** Prognostic score estimation, three ways · **3.2** Observed treatment effects across prognostic-score strata · **3.3** CATE as a function of the prognostic score, plus CART subgroup discovery by baseline prognosis |
| **Part IV. Randomization-based inference for ITE quantiles** | Unit shuffle and sign convention · one-sided confidence intervals for the effect quantiles · two-sided intervals via Bonferroni · bounds on the fraction of patients who benefit · a second worked example on the distracted-driving trial |
| **Appendix** | References, and the cache status for that knit |

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
Results shown on individual patient data are subject to each trial's data use
agreement. The source code is openly available so the method can be applied
elsewhere.
:::
